correctness.rationale: The 2026 primary paper Eq.(1.3) indeed has susceptible multiplicative mortality noise -epsilon*sigma1*S dB1 and assumes f(0)>0. Let a=epsilon*sigma1>0. On the hypothetical event S→Lambda/mu>0, I,R→0, Ito gives d(log S)=[Lambda/S-mu-beta I/f(I)+delta R/S-a^2/2]dt-a dB1; the bracket tends -a²/2, and B1(t)/t→0 a.s., forcing log S(t)/t→-a²/2. Positive point convergence instead forces log S(t)/t→0, contradiction. On invariant face I=R=0 the zero-current stationary equation (a²s²p)'=2(Lambda-mu s)p integrates to InvGamma(k=1+2mu/a²,q=2Lambda/a²), normalized on (0,infinity). Moments are q/(k-1)=Lambda/mu and q²/[(k-1)²(k-2)]=Lambda²a²/[mu²(2mu-a²)] when mu>a²/2. With a=9/20,Lambda=1,mu=1/5 compute k=241/81,q=800/81, mean=5 and variance=2025/79 exactly. Source Theorem3.2 proves time averages, which remain consistent with the finding. Neither eventual interior-to-boundary convergence in law nor almost-sure convergence of S to a random constant is claimed.
